description: A chief legal officer must approve a proposed patent license to HelioGrid and finalize its territory, field of use, royalty, exclusivity, and sublicensing terms, with input from patent counsel and the technology licensing lead.

shared_context.S1: The company has developed a battery-management technology covered by a portfolio of issued patents.
shared_context.S2: HelioGrid has proposed a ten-year worldwide exclusive license with a 5% royalty on net sales and unrestricted sublicensing.
shared_context.S3: The proposed license is intended to support HelioGrid's commercial deployment of the technology.
shared_context.S4: Under the legal department's pre-approval routine, patent counsel and the technology licensing lead each give a status update before Maya Chen makes the final approval decision.

PF1.text: Thomas reviewed the latest patent-maintenance records and confirmed that enforceable portfolio coverage for this license currently exists only in the United States and Germany; he also confirmed that the maintenance fee for US Patent 11-482901 is due in 9 days. He retrieved these records after the draft was circulated and has not yet added them to the patent schedule.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed in a call with HelioGrid's commercial sponsor that the approved business term sheet permits exclusivity only for grid-scale battery storage, sets the royalty at exactly 6% of net sales, and prohibits sublicensing; HelioGrid will not sign on the broader draft terms. She has not entered the call terms into the deal tracker yet.

acceptance_conditions: The licensed territories must be exactly the United States and Germany.
The license must require payment of the US Patent 11-482901 maintenance fee within 9 days.
Exclusivity must be limited to grid-scale battery storage.
The royalty must be exactly 6% of net sales.

content_checks.C3: any(c['type'] == 'maintenance_fee_payment' and c['target'] == 'US Patent 11-482901' and c['detail'] == 'Pay maintenance fee within 9 days' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The patent-maintenance records change the territory from the draft's worldwide grant to exactly the United States and Germany, and change the execution plan by requiring payment of the US Patent 11-482901 fee within 9 days.

HelioGrid's approved term sheet changes the commercial package from worldwide exclusivity at 5% with unrestricted sublicensing to exclusivity only for grid-scale battery storage at exactly 6% with sublicensing prohibited.
